titleEn: When the Sun Goes Down, Sleep Tight!

pages.text: "No! I won't lie down! I'll keep running!" Moya raced on the red dirt path. The sun was half behind the rocky hill, and the sky orange. Holding back a yawn, Moya called, "Just a little longer!"
Mom approached gently. "The sun has set, Moya. Time to lie down." "I'm not sleepy at all!" Moya shook their head and ran another lap.
But their eyes kept closing. Their legs shook and their hooves stumbled. A huge yawn escaped. "Am I... a little sleepy?" Their eyes felt sore.
Nia came slowly from the acacia shade. "I'm lying down now, too." Nia rubbed their eyes and yawned. Mom smiled. "Let's all get ready together!"
Bedtime had steps. First, a drink! Moya and Nia bent over the waterhole side by side. Gulp, gulp. They laughed at each other's wet noses.
Second, into the middle of the herd! Zebras lay in a circle. Moya settled beside Mom in its center. The herd was a blanket. Mom nuzzled Moya and sang, "When the sun goes down, sleep tight..."
Third, sleep beside Mom! The sun disappeared and the grassland grew dark. With the herd around, it wasn't scary. Nia folded their long neck beside Moya. Mom nuzzled Nia's back and sang again.
Now Moya sang softly to Nia. "When the sun goes down, sleep tight..." Moya stretched their neck, then rested it beside Mom. Helping Nia sleep felt good.
Moya knew the bedtime steps. "One, a sip of water! Two, into the herd! Three, lie beside Mom and sleep tight!" Only soft breathing filled the grassland. Stars twinkled.
The sun rose! Moya sprang up and stretched, feeling wonderfully light. Mom laid her neck over Moya's in a hug. "A good sleep makes morning sparkle!" Now Moya liked sunset, too.
